Chessmate

Play chess.com with your voice. Say your move, and Chessmate plays it. Go to puzzles, start a game and press buttons by voice too, so a whole game needs no mouse.

  1. Add Chessmate to Chrome
  2. Turn the microphone on

1 One time only

Add Chessmate to Chrome

You need Google Chrome on a computer and a microphone. The one built into a laptop is fine.

  1. Open Chessmate in the Chrome Web Store

    Open the Chrome Web Store page

  2. Click “Add to Chrome”
    Chessmate
    Play chess.com by voice
    Add to Chrome
  3. Click “Add extension”

    Chrome asks first. Chessmate only works on chess.com, which is why that is the site it lists.

    Add “Chessmate”?

    It can:
    Read and change your data on www.chess.com
    CancelAdd extension
  4. Pin the icon (handy, not required)

    Click the puzzle piece at the top right of Chrome, then the pin next to Chessmate. Its green pawn then stays in view, so you can see when the microphone is on.

    chess.com

    Extensions

    Chessmate
2 Each time you play

Turn the microphone on

  1. Open chess.com

    Any page works: a game, a puzzle, a lesson or the home page.

  2. Press these three keys together
    WindowsAlt+Shift+M
    Mac⌥ Option+⇧ Shift+M

    Or click Chessmate’s green pawn at the top right of Chrome.

  3. The first time, allow the microphone

    Chrome asks once. Choose Allow while visiting the site, so it never asks again.

    www.chess.com wants to

    Use your microphone
    Allow while visiting the siteAllow this timeNever allow
  4. Look for the red “on”

    A small red on on the pawn means Chessmate is listening. The Chessmate panel appears on the page and says Listening. Say a move.

    chess.comon
✋

That key press is the only one you need. The microphone stays on as you go from page to page, and even after the page reloads, until you say stop listening or press the keys again.

Three keys at once hard on the hands? Pick an easier pair: open chrome://extensions/shortcuts in the address bar and set a new shortcut for Chessmate. Chrome needs it to include Ctrl or Alt (on a Mac, ⌘, Ctrl or ⌥).

3 Playing

Say your moves

The easiest way: say the square the piece is on, then the square it goes to.

Say
What happens
e2 to e4
Moves the piece on e2 to e4
knight f3 e4
Moves by piece name, or just the square
bishop takes c6
Captures
castle kingside long castle
Castles
e8 queen
Promotes a pawn
g1 then f3
Picks up a piece, then puts it down

When two pieces can go to the same square

Chessmate marks both and asks which one. Answer with the square it starts on, like b1. Nothing moves until you answer.

When it isn’t sure what you said

It asks, for example Did you mean Nf3? Say yes to play it or cancel to drop it. Chessmate never plays a move it only guessed, and never an illegal one.

When a letter gets misheard

B, D, E and G sound alike. Say the word instead:

alpha a
bravo b
charlie c
delta d
echo e
foxtrot f
golf g
hotel h
⏱

You can say your next move while your opponent is still thinking. Chessmate waits and plays it the moment it is your turn.

4 Between games

Get around chess.com

Say where to go, or the name of the button to press.

Say
What happens
puzzles lessons bots home daily puzzle
Goes to that page
10 minutes 3 plus 2 blitz
Looks for a live game against a person, at that speed
start next continue
Starts a bot game or a lesson, or goes to the next puzzle
hint retry solution
The puzzle buttons
rematch new game review
The buttons after a game
resign then yes
Resigns. It always asks first.
close
Closes a pop-up
5 Putting it together

A whole game, hands-free

Here is a game against a computer opponent, from start to finish, with no mouse. Press the keys once at the start.

Youbots
ChessmateOpens the page of computer opponents.
Youstart
ChessmatePresses Play. The game begins.
Youe2 to e4
ChessmatePlays e4, then waits for your opponent.
Youknight f3
ChessmatePlays Nf3. Keep going, move by move.
Yourematch
ChessmateWhen the game ends, starts another one.

Against a person

Say a speed, like 10 minutes, and chess.com finds you an opponent. Moves work the same way. Chessmate won’t leave the page during a live game, so you can’t lose one on time by mistake.

Puzzles

Say puzzles, then the move. Say hint if you are stuck, retry to try again, and next for the next puzzle.

6 Optional

Sounds, read aloud and privacy

These three icons sit at the top of the Chessmate panel. Set them once with a click, and Chessmate remembers.

Sounds (on to start with). A short tone when a move is played, when Chessmate asks a question, and when it can’t play a move. You can follow along without looking.

Read moves aloud. Chrome’s voice reads every move, yours and your opponent’s.

Speech recognition. Online, by Google, is the default and the most accurate. Offline keeps your voice on your computer: Chrome downloads the speech model once.

🔒

Chessmate never records or stores your voice, and it has no servers or tracking. The list of what you said stays in that tab and clears when you close it.

7 Help

If something goes wrong

Nothing happens when I speak
Look for the red on on the green pawn. No red on? Press Alt+Shift+M (on a Mac, ⌥+⇧+M) again.
Chrome blocked the microphone
Click the small icon at the left of the address bar on chess.com, set Microphone to Allow, then reload the page.
It hears the wrong letter
Use the letter words: bravo for b, delta for d, echo for e, golf for g. Speaking a little slower helps too.
It played nothing and made a low tone
No piece can make that move right now. The panel says why. Try another move, or say what can I say.
I want it to stop listening
Say stop listening, or press the keys again.
